summary: Great Smoky Mountains NC-side fire tower at 5,647 ft, now removed; a 2019 blog reports only foundation blocks remain.

facts.status_note: Tennessee Landforms and the trail guide both say the tower is removed. A 2019 blog says only foundation blocks remain.

access.note: The site is inside the national park and is reached on foot by the Spruce Mountain Trail. No tower stands there to climb.

visit.trail_note: Accounts disagree on the hike: 1.2 miles in and out from Balsam Mountain Road (2019 blog), or 5.5 miles along the ridge from Polls Gap (trail guide).

corrections.why: NC is the state, not a county. The trail guide files the Spruce Mountain Trail under Swain County, North Carolina. A 2010 account reaches the old site from Cataloochee, so check the county before the record is final.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2019 blog gives 1.2 miles in and out from Balsam Mountain Road; the trail guide gives 5.5 miles from Polls Gap. The sources give different starting points and lengths, so both are kept and neither is preferred.
The trail guide puts the trail in Swain County. The 2010 account reaches the old tower site from Cataloochee. No source settles the county, so the proposed correction is provisional.

sources.title: Spruce Mountain Trail, Swain County North Carolina Hiking Trails

notes_for_editor: Four sources, two of them personal hiking blogs (2010 and 2019). No source gives a build year, so no event is dated; the 2019 blog dates the tower only as four years after the park was created. Record county NC is a state code; see the correction. Clemson thesis abstract (open.clemson.edu/all_theses/1130/) was checked and does not mention Spruce Mountain. Access is inferred from the trail descriptions, not from a managing-agency statement. The record's coordinates were not checked against a source.
